data.name: TutorialWelcomeText
data.value: Your phone can now do something it never could: stream its music to the phones around you. No Wi-Fi, no internet.

data.name: TutorialPairText
data.value: Only once: pair the phones over Bluetooth (Settings › Bluetooth › Pair new device). After that, on the same Wi-Fi, the sound also goes over Wi-Fi: steadier and better quality.

data.name: TutorialBroadcastText
data.value: Whoever has the music taps “Share my sound” and accepts the permissions. Android calls it “screen recording”: that is how it lets AuraMusic capture the sound, nothing is recorded. Then play your music. Mind that some apps, like Spotify, forbid capturing their sound, and the others then hear nothing. YouTube Music works.

data.name: TutorialListenText
data.value: The others tap “Listen”: their phone finds the broadcaster on its own and reconnects if you drift apart. The screen can be off.

data.name: TutorialAnywhereText
data.value: The sound travels over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth at once: if one drops, the other takes over. No Wi-Fi around? One of you turns on their hotspot, the other joins it: you get Wi-Fi quality anywhere. The music goes from one phone to the other, never through the internet.

data.name: TutorialTipsText
data.value: Stay within a few meters. The sound arrives slightly delayed: in the same room, everyone wears headphones to avoid echo. Up to 3 or 4 phones can listen at once. Pull the home screen down to check for an update.
